concern.concern: Fact F7 states 'Linking of disjoint oriented curves is the signed intersection with a spanning two-chain' and cites thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection. That supplier's Statement instead requires a supplied compact embedded smooth spanning surface, transversality, and a regular diagram. The fact strengthens the cited interface without explaining the chain extension. Proof 2.1's actual cross-ball vanishing follows immediately from the homological linking definition because a curve bounds an integral chain in its ball, so this does not undermine the surjection.

original_concerns.reason: The signed-intersection supplier is explicitly conditional on a supplied embedded smooth spanning surface, transverse circle and diagram; it does not state the arbitrary singular-chain extension attributed in F7. Actual Proof2.1 needs only zero linking across separated balls. The existing Seifert-pairing definition defines linking as the meridian coefficient in complement homology. A cycle bounding an integral chain in its own ball is zero in the complement of the other ball, so its coefficient is zero. Replace the excessive Fact with that exact already-used homological argument; the surjection Statement and every category/choice premise stay unchanged.

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: [F7] Linking of disjoint oriented curves is the signed intersection with a spanning two-chain. [[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]]
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: [F7] For disjoint oriented curves, linking is the positive-meridian coefficient of the first curve in the homology of the complement of the second, extended additively over integral one-cycles. A cycle in a ball disjoint from the second curve bounds an integral singular two-chain in that ball, since a ball is contractible. Its complement-homology class and hence its linking coefficient are zero. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]]
